summary.intent: Resolve all open PR review comments on PR #296 (SDK extraction), fix a CI E2E test failure caused by Zustand stores not being exposed in production builds, and refactor E2E tests to reduce reliance on internal store access.
summary.outcome: All review threads across multiple review passes were resolved with code fixes. CI was unblocked by gating `__ZUSTAND_STORES` exposure behind a `VITE_E2E` build flag, then further refined to expose only a minimal `window.__E2E` helper with two getters. Vault readiness polling was replaced with UI-based waits and public key extraction was moved to read from the Settings page UI.

repo: The `__ZUSTAND_STORES` window object is only exposed under `import.meta.env.DEV`, so E2E tests that poll it silently hang forever in production CI builds.
CI E2E workflow builds the web app with `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web build` (production mode), not dev mode — `import.meta.env.DEV` is always false.
The full-workflow spec uses `test.describe.serial`, so a single failure at test 3.7 skips all 36 subsequent tests, masking downstream failures.
Release Please with multiple components uses the target branch name ('main') in the PR title instead of a version number when `pull-request-title-pattern` uses `${version}`.
The `FolderTree.clear()` method zeros all stored key buffers — callers who pass buffers into `registerFolder` without defensive copies will have their own buffers zeroed on vault destroy.

The `ensureFolderRegistered` guard added from a review comment broke uploads because SDK-created folders and root folder after vault init have valid keys but `isLoaded` may not be set in all code paths.

New packages (`core`, `api-client`, `sdk-core`, `sdk`) were missing from all three CI workflows (`e2e.yml`, `deploy-staging.yml`, `e2e-desktop.yml`) which only built `crypto` before web/desktop targets.
The crypto package correctly lists `@cipherbox/core` as a devDependency — it is only used in `vault-ipns.test.ts` for cross-package test verification, not at runtime.

code.finding: Zustand store exposure now gated behind `import.meta.env.DEV || import.meta.env.VITE_E2E === 'true'`, exposing only `window.__E2E` with `getAccessToken()` and `getRootIpnsName()` getters instead of full store hooks.
`fileKey` was not cleared if an exception occurred before the re-wrap try/catch — fixed by wrapping the entire post-upload section in try/finally with `clearBytes()`.
`createFolder` leaked plaintext `folderKey` and `ipnsPrivateKey` on failure — fixed by moving duplicate-name check before key generation and adding try/catch with `clearBytes` on failure.

`registerFolder` stored caller-owned key buffers directly; `destroy()` → `folderTree.clear()` would zero the caller's buffers. Fixed with defensive copies and returning a copy from `getFolderIpnsPrivateKey`.
The `isLoaded` guard added to `ensureFolderRegistered` was too strict — SDK-created folders never go through the store's loaded path. Guard should only check for empty key material.
Test 3.7 timeout needed to be 360s (not 240s or 180s) due to cumulative auth restore + vault + root sync + file waits totalling ~330s worst case.
Public key extraction now navigates to `/settings`, reads `.settings-pubkey-value`, validates non-empty, then navigates back — replacing Zustand store access.
Vault readiness detection replaced: no longer polls `window.__ZUSTAND_STORES?.vault?.rootFolderKey`, instead waits for file list or empty-state UI element to appear.
`requestAnimationFrame` handle needed to be hoisted out of the async IIFE to be accessible in the effect cleanup for `cancelAnimationFrame`.
Needs `VITE_E2E: 'true'` in the web build env vars to enable `window.__E2E` exposure in the E2E build.

workflow: When a PR has `test.describe.serial` tests, the first failure hides all subsequent failures — always check the full failure list from the last green run, not just the reported failure.
Vite bakes `VITE_*` env vars at compile time, enabling tree-shaking of test-only code from production bundles when the var is absent.

Release Please multi-component manifests: `pull-request-title-pattern` must be set at the top level (outside `packages`) to affect the combined PR title; `${version}` is meaningless when multiple packages have different versions.
When a PR is already merged, CI workflow fixes must be cherry-picked or re-applied on a new branch from main — they won't be included via the original branch.
Resolving GitHub review threads requires two separate API calls: a REST call to post the reply comment, then a GraphQL mutation to mark the thread resolved.

friction: The `isLoaded` guard added from a legitimate Copilot review comment immediately broke uploads in CI — the review comment's suggested fix was architecturally incorrect for the actual code paths.
CI E2E build failure was caused by `__ZUSTAND_STORES` being silently undefined in production builds — no runtime error, just an infinite wait, making root cause non-obvious.
CI workflow fixes were committed to the already-merged PR branch and never reached main, requiring a second branch and PR to re-apply the same changes.
The `recycle-bin.spec.ts` uses `__ZUSTAND_STORES__` (double underscore suffix) — a different variable name from `__ZUSTAND_STORES`, creating a subtle inconsistency.
The orval-generated `VaultResponseDtoInitializedAt` type is wrong but regenerating produces the same incorrect output — an upstream orval bug with nullable Date types.
TypeScript's strict `Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>` vs `BlobPart` type incompatibility required a `as BlobPart` cast after the `.buffer` removal fix.
Background test runs via `run_in_background` required polling `TaskOutput` to check completion status, adding workflow friction.
open_items: Concurrent mutations to the same folder (Thread 2 from first review pass) — acknowledged as out of scope; UI-level serialization handles it for now, but a proper architectural fix is deferred.
The `web3auth-helpers.ts` file still uses `__ZUSTAND_STORES` for the legacy email-based test login flow — it's dead code for current wallet-based tests but hasn't been removed.
The `recycle-bin.spec.ts` uses a different variable `__ZUSTAND_STORES__` (double underscore suffix) — unclear if this is intentional or a bug; not addressed.

Test 3.7 (session restore after reload) remains sensitive to Sapphire Devnet latency on CI — the root cause (Core Kit TSS key export slowness) is not fixed, only the timeout and store-polling issues were addressed.

The conflict-detection tests still use `window.__E2E` (requiring `VITE_E2E` flag) — could potentially be replaced with in-browser `page.evaluate(() => fetch(...))` calls using session cookies, eliminating the need for the flag entirely.
